topic.title: Reinforcement Learning across Time Scales and Task Structure
topic.overview: Reinforcement learning must connect delayed outcomes with decisions made at different levels and speeds. This cluster brings together early adaptive networks, temporally structured models, hierarchical learning, coordinated behavior, and adaptation to changing environments. It also examines tasks where rewarding outcomes are rare, making exploration difficult even when a reward can be verified.
topic.whyItMatters: The timing of interaction is part of the learning problem when the world keeps changing during computation. Likewise, decomposing a task into useful temporal units can affect which experiences are available. These issues complicate comparisons based only on episode counts or final reward.
topic.evolution: A 1987 adaptive-automata model studies learning from a shared reinforcement signal across hidden elements. Historical titles extend toward variable temporal resolution and hierarchical control. A 2023 study explicitly balances policy-training time against environmental change, while a 2025 mathematical case study analyzes the difficulty of finding rare, highly rewarded instances.
openQuestions: How should an agent divide time between learning and acting in a changing environment?
Which temporal abstractions make rare rewards easier to discover without hiding essential decisions?
